newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FAI concerned about scrapped N.Z. sale.
newsitem.headline: FAI concerned about scrapped N.Z. sale.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd chief executive Rodney Adler said on Thursday that he was concerned about the possible impact of the abandoned sale of its New Zealand and Pacific islands general insurance unit on staff and the company's reputation in the region.

Adler said Australian Stock Exchange disclosure rules meant the sale talks had to be revealed when the sale was not guaranteed. He said FAI had no intention of selling the profitable unit until it was approached with a top-price A$50 million offer from rival insurer MMI Ltd.
MMI is 38 percent-owned by Germany's Allianz AG and last December hired senior FAI executive Angus MacIver as its head of international operations.
"After contemplating it (the MMI ofer) the acquiring party withdrew so now I have 100 staff, I have a fabulous brand name in New Zealand which has sustained damage," he told Reuters.
"I just find the whole thing embarrassing."

Adler said he had written to the ASX to complain about the disclosure rules which led to the tentative deal being announced to the market on July 7 with completion set for early August after due diligence and regulatory approval.

The statement said the offer price was significantly above the unit's carrying value and the funds could be better used to achieve growth in the Asian region where national and regional economies were stronger.
"I guarantee you, sadly, that we will lose some senior staff that will say 'oh well eventually FAI is going to sell us anyway". And we weren't, it wasn't our intention," Adler said.
Adler said the N.Z. unit was expected to achieve earnings of between NZ$6 million and NZ$7 million in the 1996/97 (July/June) just ended.
He said a report about the failed transaction in the Wednesday edition of The Australian newspaper was accurate.

The report said MMI had reduced its offer to about A$45 million once the sale had been revealed in a statement to the stock exchange. It also said the disclosure had been sought by MMI's lawyers and opposed by FAI's.
MMI managing director Pieter Franzen was overseas and not available to comment until next week, his office said.
The two companies said on Tuesday the deal had been terminated by mutual agreement as they could not agree on the final purchase price. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
